title: Order-to-Consumption Lag for Pantry Goods
dataSources: Amazon order records (`amazon:order`), meal-plan inventory (`mealplan:item`), and pharmacy refill events (`pharmacy:refill`).
app: Household logistics telemetry from Amazon order history, meal-plan inventory tools, and pharmacy refill portals sent to Splunk HEC via exports and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=mealplan:item
| search consume_delay_days=*
| stats avg(consume_delay_days) as avg_consume_delay_days perc90(consume_delay_days) as p90_consume_delay_days count as samples by category
| sort 0 - avg_consume_delay_days
value: Lag from purchase to use shows which goods are being stocked thoughtfully and which are just sitting.
implementation: Send the relevant duration field for order-to-consumption lag to `index=personal` and review both average and p90 latency instead of relying on single examples.
visualization: Table of average and p90 order-to-consumption lag.
grandmaExplanation: It blends how long order-to-consumption lag usually takes, so slowdowns are obvious instead of anecdotal.
